paragraphs: R' Yudan, son of R' Shimon ben Yochai’s daughter.

In Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin (Hyman cites chapter 1, ה״ד-יו), R’ Chiya bar Ba cites R’ Yudan, the son of R’ Shimon ben Yochai’s daughter, reciting Shimon ben Yochai’s teaching. But Hyman says that in truth it should read as in Peah, at the beginning of chapter 1, locator 3: Rabbi Chiya bar Va cites Rabbi Yudan bar Dorati, saying that the teaching is Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai’s.
Penei Moshe reads this way in Kiddushin as well, according to Hyman.

notes.text: Bar beratei means daughter’s son; it is not a personal name Beratya. Hyman proposes bar Dorati instead. The retrieved Peah text retains bar beratei in brackets, so it does not independently establish Hyman’s proposed alternative. The supplied Kiddushin locator and patronym remain source questions.

The saved whole Venice Peah 1:1 scalar explicitly reads Rabbi Chiyya bar Va and Rabbi Yudan BEN Dorati, and calls the teaching Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai's. It supplies a Dorati witness that the earlier bracketed bar-beratei comparison did not, without deleting that other edition. Hyman has BAR Dorati, not Venice BEN. Daughter's son is a maternal relationship, not the invented personal name Beratya or school membership. Hyman's IN TRUTH SHOULD READ instruction retains its force and attribution. Kiddushin's added יו, Peah's trailing ג, and the Penei Moshe reading claim remain unverified; no genealogy or correction history is automatically admitted. The uninspected maternal-chain title occurrences remain R'.

The matching passage in the consulted Kiddushin is 1:7:13 and gives the maternal relationship. In Peah 1:1:30, the digital Venice text reads ben Dorati, while Guggenheimer’s Hebrew gives the maternal wording in brackets. Penei Moshe on Peah refers readers to Kiddushin and has ben Torati, spelled with a tav. The consulted Penei Moshe at the Kiddushin passage comments on the teaching about honoring parents without restating the name. Hyman’s reported reading in Kiddushin remains attributed to him.
